notes.md:
# Ancient India

## 1. Harappan (Indus) civilisation (c. 2600–1900 BCE)
| Site | Discoverer | Famous for |
|---|---|---|
| Harappa (Punjab, Pak.) | Daya Ram Sahni, 1921 | granaries |
| **Mohenjo-daro** (Sindh) | R. D. Banerji, 1922 | **Great Bath**, great granary, dancing girl, priest-king |
| **Lothal** (Gujarat) | S. R. Rao | **dockyard** |
| Kalibangan (Rajasthan) | B. B. Lal, B. K. Thapar | ploughed field, fire altars |
| Dholavira (Gujarat) | R. S. Bisht | water reservoirs, signboard (UNESCO 2021) |
| Rakhigarhi (Haryana) | | largest Indian site |

## 2. Vedic age
Rigveda – oldest (10 mandalas, Gayatri mantra); Samaveda – music; Yajurveda – rituals; Atharvaveda – medicine, charms. *Satyameva Jayate* – Mundaka Upanishad. Varna system; sabha & samiti.

## 3. Mahajanapadas and new religions
- 16 Mahajanapadas; **Magadha** rose under Haryanka (Bimbisara, Ajatashatru) → Shishunaga → **Nanda** → Maurya.
- **Buddhism** – Gautama Buddha (b. Lumbini; enlightenment Bodh Gaya; first sermon Sarnath – *Dharmachakrapravartana*; death Kushinagar). Councils: Rajagriha, Vaishali, **Pataliputra (Ashoka)**, Kashmir (Kanishka).
- **Jainism** – Mahavira, 24th tirthankara (Rishabhanatha 1st). Five vows; Shvetambara / Digambara (Bhadrabahu went south with Chandragupta Maurya → Shravanabelagola).

## 4. Mauryas (321–185 BCE)
Chandragupta Maurya (with **Kautilya** – *Arthashastra*; Megasthenes – *Indica*) → Bindusara → **Ashoka** (Kalinga war 261 BCE; dhamma; edicts in Brahmi, Kharosthi; Karnataka edicts at **Maski** (named 'Ashoka'), Brahmagiri, Siddapura). Lion Capital of **Sarnath** = national emblem.

## 5. After the Mauryas
Shungas (Pushyamitra) · Satavahanas · Indo-Greeks (Menander – *Milinda Panho*) · **Kushanas (Kanishka – Shaka era 78 CE; Gandhara & Mathura art)** · Sangam age (Cheras, Cholas, Pandyas; Tamil Sangam literature).

## 6. Guptas (c. 320–550 CE) – 'Golden Age'
Chandragupta I (married Licchavi princess Kumaradevi) → **Samudragupta** ('Napoleon of India', Allahabad pillar – Harishena) → **Chandragupta II** (Vikramaditya; Fa-Hien visited; Navaratnas incl. Kalidasa) → Kumaragupta (**Nalanda**) → Skandagupta (repelled Huns). Aryabhata (*Aryabhatiya*), Varahamihira, Ajanta paintings.

## 7. Harsha (606–647)
Capital Kannauj; **Hiuen Tsang** visited; Banabhatta – *Harshacharita*; defeated by **Pulakeshin II** on the Narmada.

## 8. South India
Pallavas of Kanchi (Mahendravarman I – *Mattavilasa Prahasana*; Narasimhavarman I – Mamallapuram rathas) vs Chalukyas of Badami.

## ⚠ Traps
- The dockyard is at **Lothal**, the Great Bath at **Mohenjo-daro**.
- Order of Magadha dynasties: **Haryanka → Shishunaga → Nanda → Maurya → Shunga**.
- Fa-Hien → Chandragupta II; Hiuen Tsang → Harsha; Megasthenes → Chandragupta Maurya.

notes.md:
# Medieval India

## 1. Early invasions
Muhammad bin Qasim – Sindh (712) · **Mahmud of Ghazni** – 17 raids (1000–1027), Somnath 1025; Al-Biruni (*Kitab-ul-Hind*) · **Muhammad Ghori** – Tarain I (1191, lost to Prithviraj Chauhan), **Tarain II (1192, won)**.

## 2. Delhi Sultanate (1206–1526)
| Dynasty | Key rulers and facts |
|---|---|
| Slave / Mamluk | **Qutb-ud-din Aibak** (founder, began Qutub Minar) · **Iltutmish** (real consolidator, completed Qutub Minar, silver *tanka* & copper *jital*, iqta) · **Razia Sultan** (only woman ruler) · **Balban** (sijda, paibos, 'Zil-i-Ilahi') |
| Khalji | **Alauddin Khalji** – market control (*Sera-i-Adl* for cloth/manufactured goods), *dagh* & *huliya*, Malik Kafur's southern raids; Amir Khusrau ('Tuti-i-Hind') |
| Tughlaq | **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** – capital to Daulatabad, token currency, Ibn Battuta · **Firoz Shah** – canals, towns **Hisar, Fatehabad**, Jaunpur, Firozabad; jizya on Brahmins · Timur's invasion 1398 |
| Sayyid | |
| Lodi | Bahlul Lodi (founder) · **Sikandar Lodi – founded Agra (1504)** · Ibrahim Lodi – lost Panipat I (1526) |

## 3. Mughals
| Ruler | Highlights |
|---|---|
| **Babur** | Panipat I 1526, Khanwa 1527; *Baburnama* (Turki); tomb **Kabul** |
| Humayun | lost to Sher Shah at Chausa (1539) & Kannauj (1540); *Humayun-nama* by Gulbadan Begum |
| **Sher Shah Suri** | rupiya, Grand Trunk Road, tomb Sasaram |
| **Akbar** | Panipat II 1556 (Bairam Khan vs Hemu); mansabdari; **Todar Mal – zabt & dahsala**; Din-i-Ilahi 1582; Buland Darwaza (Gujarat victory); Navaratnas – **Abul Fazl & brother Faizi**, Birbal, Tansen; tomb **Sikandra** |
| Jahangir | chain of justice; Nur Jahan; Sir Thomas Roe; tomb **Shahdara, Lahore** |
| **Shah Jahan** | Taj Mahal, Red Fort & Jama Masjid (Delhi), Peacock Throne |
| **Aurangzeb** | reimposed jizya 1679; Deccan wars; *Bibi ka Maqbara* (his son) |
| Bahadur Shah II | last emperor, exiled to **Rangoon** (1858) |

## 4. Marathas
**Shivaji** – coronation Raigad 1674; Ashtapradhan; taxes **chauth (¼) & sardeshmukhi (1/10)**; Pratapgad 1659 (Afzal Khan), **Salher 1672** (over Mughals); southern expedition 1676–79 allied with **Qutb Shahi of Golconda**. Successors: **Sambhaji → Rajaram → Shivaji II (Tarabai) → Shahu**. Peshwas: **Balaji Vishwanath → Baji Rao I → Balaji Baji Rao (Nana Saheb) → Madhav Rao I**. Panipat III 1761 vs Ahmad Shah Abdali.

## 5. South India and the Deccan
- **Vijayanagara** (1336): Sangama → Saluva → **Tuluva** (Krishnadevaraya – *Amuktamalyada*, Ashtadiggajas) → Aravidu. **Talikota 1565**. Travellers: Nicolo de Conti (Italy), **Abdur Razzaq** (Persia), **Domingo Paes, Fernão Nuniz** (Portugal), Afanasy Nikitin (Russia, Bahmani).
- **Bahmani** (1347, Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah, Gulbarga → Bidar; Mahmud Gawan). Five successor sultanates: **Bijapur (Yusuf Adil Shah)**, **Ahmadnagar (Malik Ahmad Nizam Shah)**, **Berar (Fathullah Imad Shah)**, **Golconda (Quli Qutb Shah)**, Bidar (Barid Shah). Bijapur's Ibrahim Adil Shah I made **Dakhni** the court language.
- Cholas: Rajaraja I (Brihadeeswara, Thanjavur), Rajendra I (Gangaikonda Cholapuram, Srivijaya expedition); **Uttaramerur** inscriptions on village elections. Kakatiyas: **Rudramadevi**, Warangal; Ramappa temple (UNESCO 2021).

## 6. Bhakti and Sufi
Alvars (Vishnu) & Nayanars (Shiva) · **Shankara (8th c.) → Ramanuja (Vishishtadvaita) → Basavanna (12th c.) → Madhva (Dvaita, 13th c.)** · Kabir · Guru Nanak · Mirabai · Tulsidas · Chaitanya (Bengal) · Jnaneshwar (Maharashtra) · Shankaradeva (Assam) · Purandaradasa & Kanakadasa. Sufi orders: **Chishti** (Muinuddin – Ajmer; Nizamuddin Auliya – Delhi; **Bande Nawaz – Kalaburagi**), Suhrawardi, Naqshbandi, **Qadiri (Dara Shikoh)**.

## ⚠ Traps
- Iltutmish was Aibak's **son-in-law**, not his son.
- Panipat I 1526, II 1556, III 1761.
- Mohammed Gawan was executed by **Muhammad Shah III**.

notes.md:
# Modern India and the freedom struggle

## 1. British expansion
| Event | Year | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Battle of **Plassey** | 1757 | Clive vs Siraj-ud-Daulah (Mir Jafar's betrayal) |
| Battle of **Buxar** | 1764 | → Treaty of Allahabad 1765: **Diwani** of Bengal, Bihar, Orissa |
| Regulating Act | 1773 | Warren Hastings first Governor-General of Bengal; Supreme Court Calcutta 1774 |
| **Permanent Settlement** | 1793 | **Cornwallis**; Bengal, Bihar, Orissa; zamindars hereditary owners; ~10/11 of rent to the Company |
| Ryotwari | 1792 / 1820 | **Alexander Read** (Baramahal), **Thomas Munro** (Madras) |
| Mahalwari | 1822 | Holt Mackenzie (NW Provinces) |
| Subsidiary Alliance | 1798 | **Wellesley**; Hyderabad first |
| Doctrine of Lapse | 1848–56 | **Dalhousie**; Satara first; first railway Bombay–Thane 1853 |
| Revolt of 1857 | 10 May 1857 | began at **Meerut**; greased cartridges; Mangal Pandey (Barrackpore) |
| Govt of India Act | 1858 | Crown rule; Canning first Viceroy |

**1857 leaders:** Delhi – Bahadur Shah II · Lucknow – Begum Hazrat Mahal · Kanpur – Nana Saheb (Tantia Tope) · Jhansi – Rani Lakshmibai · Jagdishpur – Kunwar Singh.

**Viceroys:** Lytton (Vernacular Press Act 1878, Delhi Durbar 1877) · **Ripon** (repealed it; local self-government 1882; First Factory Act 1881; Rendition of Mysore 1881; Ilbert Bill) · Curzon (Partition of Bengal 1905) · Minto (Morley–Minto 1909) · Chelmsford (1919 reforms, Jallianwala) · Irwin (Gandhi–Irwin Pact 1931) · Linlithgow (August Offer 1940, Cripps 1942) · Wavell (Simla 1945) · Mountbatten (3 June Plan 1947). Last Governor-General: **C. Rajagopalachari** (1948–50).

## 2. Social and religious reform
| Reformer | Organisation / work |
|---|---|
| Raja Ram Mohan Roy | Brahmo Samaj (1828); Sati abolished 1829 (Bentinck) |
| Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar | Widow Remarriage Act 1856 |
| J. E. D. Bethune | first Hindu girls' school, Calcutta (1849) |
| Dayananda Saraswati | Arya Samaj (1875), *Satyarth Prakash*, 'Back to the Vedas' |
| Jyotiba Phule | Satyashodhak Samaj (1873), *Gulamgiri* (dedicated to the US anti-slavery activists) |
| Swami Vivekananda | Ramakrishna Mission (1897); Chicago 1893 |
| Sir Syed Ahmad Khan | MAO College, Aligarh (1875) |
| Sri Narayana Guru | 'One caste, one religion, one God for man' |

## 3. Early national movement
- Pre-Congress bodies: British Indian Association, **East India Association (Dadabhai Naoroji, London 1866)**, **Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (Ranade)**, Madras Mahajana Sabha, **Indian Association (Surendranath Banerjee)**.
- **INC 1885** – A. O. Hume; first session Bombay, president **W. C. Bonnerjee**. Surat split 1907 (president Rash Behari Ghosh). First woman president **Annie Besant (Calcutta 1917)**. **Lahore 1929 – Nehru, Purna Swaraj**. Belgaum 1924 – Gandhi.
- **Swadeshi Movement – 7 Aug 1905** (→ National Handloom Day). Muslim League 1906 (Dacca). Home Rule Leagues 1916 (Tilak, Besant). Lucknow Pact 1916.

## 4. Gandhian era
| Event | Year |
|---|---|
| Gandhi in South Africa (Dada Abdulla's case) | 1893 |
| Return to India – Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (9 Jan) | 1915 |
| Champaran / Kheda / Ahmedabad | 1917 / 1918 |
| Rowlatt Act; **Jallianwala Bagh** (13 April, Gen. Dyer) | 1919 |
| Khilafat + Non-Cooperation | 1920–22 |
| Chauri Chaura → withdrawal | Feb 1922 |
| Swaraj Party | 1923 |
| Simon Commission ('Simon Go Back'; Lala Lajpat Rai died) | 1927–28 |
| Nehru Report | 1928 |
| Purna Swaraj; Independence Day 26 Jan 1930 | 1929–30 |
| **Dandi March** 12 Mar – 6 Apr | 1930 |
| Gandhi–Irwin Pact; 2nd RTC | 1931 |
| **Communal Award (Aug) → Poona Pact (Sept) → 3rd RTC (Nov)** | 1932 |
| August Offer · Individual Satyagraha | 1940 |
| Cripps Mission · **Quit India (8 Aug, 'Do or Die')** | 1942 |
| INA / Azad Hind government (Bose) | 1943 |
| Cabinet Mission · **Direct Action Day (16 Aug)** | 1946 |
| Attlee's announcement (20 Feb) · Mountbatten Plan (3 June) · Independence | 1947 |

Influences on Gandhi: **Tolstoy, Ruskin (*Unto This Last*), Raychandbhai**, Thoreau. Rash Behari Bose escaped to **Japan** (1915). Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, Sukhdev hanged 23 Mar 1931.

## ⚠ Traps
- First INC president: **W. C. Bonnerjee**, not A. O. Hume.
- Permanent Settlement was in **Bengal**, not the south; Ryotwari in the south.
- August Offer **1940** (not 1939); Communal Award came **before** the Poona Pact.
- Last Governor-General of India: **Rajagopalachari**; of British India: Mountbatten.

notes.md:
# Karnataka – history, culture and art

## 1. Dynasties
| Dynasty | Founder / great rulers | Capital | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Satavahanas | Simuka | Paithan | early Deccan |
| **Kadambas** (345) | **Mayurasharma**; Kakusthavarma | **Banavasi** | first Kannada kingdom; **Halmidi inscription** (c. 450) – earliest Kannada inscription |
| **Western Gangas** | Konganivarma | Talakadu | **Chavundaraya** (minister) built the **Gommateshwara statue, Shravanabelagola** (983) |
| **Chalukyas of Badami** | Pulakeshin I; **Pulakeshin II** (defeated Harsha on the Narmada; Aihole inscription by Ravikirti) | **Badami (Vatapi)** | rock-cut caves at Badami (**sandstone**), temples at **Aihole** ('cradle of Indian temple architecture'), **Pattadakal** (UNESCO) |
| **Rashtrakutas** | **Dantidurga**; Krishna I (Kailasa temple, Ellora); **Amoghavarsha I** | Manyakheta (Malkhed) | *Kavirajamarga*; emblem **Garuda** |
| **Chalukyas of Kalyani** | Taila II; **Vikramaditya VI** (Vikrama era) | Kalyani | Bilhana, Vijnaneshwara (*Mitakshara*) |
| **Hoysalas** | Sala; **Vishnuvardhana**; Veera Ballala II | Belur, **Dwarasamudra (Halebidu)** | soapstone star-shaped temples; Queen **Shantala**; Ramanuja converted Vishnuvardhana |
| **Vijayanagara** (1336) | Harihara I & Bukka I; **Krishnadevaraya** | **Hampi** | Talikota 1565 |
| Bahmani (1347) | Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah | Gulbarga → Bidar | Mahmud Gawan's madrasa |
| Adil Shahis | Yusuf Adil Shah | Bijapur | **Gol Gumbaz** (Mohammed Adil Shah) |
| Keladi Nayakas | Chowdappa Nayaka; **Rani Chennamma**, Shivappa Nayaka | Ikkeri, Bidanur | Shivappa Nayaka's *shist* revenue system |
| **Wodeyars of Mysore** | Yaduraya (1399); Raja Wodeyar (Srirangapatna 1610, Dasara); Chikka Devaraja; **Krishnaraja Wodeyar III** (Mummadi); **Nalvadi Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV** – 'Golden Age' | Mysuru | Diwans: Rangacharlu, **Sheshadri Iyer**, **Visvesvaraya**, Mirza Ismail |
| Hyder Ali & Tipu Sultan | | Srirangapatna | four Anglo-Mysore wars; Tipu died 1799 |

**Hoysala temples:** Chennakeshava, Belur – *ekakuta*; Hoysaleshwara, Halebidu – *dwikuta*; Veeranarayana, Belavadi – *trikuta*; Lakshmi Devi, Doddagaddavalli – *chatushkuta*; Keshava, Somanathapura (Narasimha III). Belur, Halebidu and Somanathapura are UNESCO sites (2023). **Ghatikas** were centres of learning.

**Badami caves:** cave 1 Shaiva · cave 2 Vaishnava · cave 3 Vaishnava (largest, 578 CE, Mangalesha) · cave 4 Jaina.

## 2. Mysore State, modern era
- Rendition (1881): power restored to the Wodeyars; **Representative Assembly (1881)** under Rangacharlu.
- Sheshadri Iyer (1883–1901): Mysore civil service exam, agriculture dept, Oriental Library, Shivanasamudra hydro-electric project (1902, Asia's first).
- Visvesvaraya: KRS dam, Mysore University (1916), State Bank of Mysore (1913), Bhadravati iron works, Engineers' Day 15 Sept.
- **First co-operative society: Kanaginahal (Gadag), 1905 – Siddanagouda Sanna Ramanagouda Patil**, father of the co-operative movement.
- Printing presses: Basel Mission – Mangaluru (1841); Government Press – Bengaluru; Ambavilasa – Mysuru; Subuddhi Prakasha – Belagavi.

## 3. Freedom struggle in Karnataka
| Event | Year |
|---|---|
| Kittur Rani Chennamma's revolt; Sangolli Rayanna hanged 1831 | 1824 |
| Belgaum Congress session – the only one presided by Gandhi | 1924 |
| Ankola salt satyagraha | 1930 |
| Shivapura flag satyagraha (Mandya) | Apr 1938 |
| **Vidurashwatha firing** (Kolar) | 25 Apr 1938 |
| Isur (Shivamogga) – declared itself free in Quit India | 1942 |
| **Mysore Chalo** for responsible government | 1947 |
| Unification as **Mysore State** | 1 Nov 1956 |
| Renamed **Karnataka** (D. Devaraj Urs) | 1 Nov 1973 |

Unification leaders: **Aluru Venkata Rao** ('Kannada Kulapurohita'), Hardekar Manjappa, S. Nijalingappa. Newspaper **Pauravani** (from Hindupur) supported responsible government.

## 4. Culture
- Folk arts: Yakshagana, Dollu Kunitha, Veeragase, Kamsale, Bhoota Kola, Huli Vesha; festivals: Mysuru Dasara, Karaga, Kambala, Hampi Utsav.
- Murals: Badami (Chalukya), Lepakshi (Vijayanagara); Mysore painting (gesso work).
- Haridasas: Purandaradasa ('father of Carnatic music'), Kanakadasa. Vachana movement: Basavanna, Allama Prabhu, Akka Mahadevi.

## ⚠ Traps
- Earliest Kannada inscription: **Halmidi** (Kadamba); earliest work: *Kavirajamarga* (Rashtrakuta).
- Badami cave 3 is Vaishnava, not Shaiva.
- Mysore State was renamed Karnataka in **1973**, not 1956.

notes.title: World history timeline – revision notes
notes.md:
# Chronology of world history

## 1. Prehistory (order of ages)
**Palaeolithic (Old Stone) → Mesolithic → Neolithic (farming, polished tools) → Chalcolithic (copper + stone) → Bronze Age → Iron Age.**

## 2. Ancient world
| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| c. 3200 BCE | **Cuneiform** writing in **Sumer (Mesopotamia)**; hieroglyphs in Egypt |
| c. 2560 BCE | **Great Pyramid of Giza** (Khufu) – the only surviving ancient wonder |
| c. 1754 BCE | **Code of Hammurabi**, Babylon |
| 776 BCE | First ancient **Olympic Games** (Olympia, Greece) |
| 753 BCE | Legendary founding of **Rome** |
| 508 BCE | **Democracy** at Athens (Cleisthenes) |
| 490 BCE | Battle of Marathon (Greeks v. Persians) |
| 326 / 323 BCE | Alexander defeats Porus (Hydaspes) / dies at Babylon |
| 221 BCE | **Qin Shi Huang** unifies China; Great Wall linked |
| 44 BCE | Julius Caesar assassinated |
| 27 BCE | **Augustus** – first Roman emperor |
| 476 CE | Fall of the **Western Roman Empire** |
| 622 CE | **Hijra** – start of the Islamic calendar |
| 800 CE | **Charlemagne** crowned emperor |

**Seven ancient wonders:** Great Pyramid of Giza, Hanging Gardens of Babylon, Temple of Artemis (Diana) at Ephesus, Statue of Zeus at Olympia, Mausoleum at Halicarnassus, Colossus of Rhodes, Lighthouse (Pharos) of Alexandria – **only the Pyramid survives**.

## 3. Medieval to early modern
| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| 1066 | Norman Conquest of England (Battle of Hastings) |
| 1215 | **Magna Carta** (King John) |
| 1337–1453 | **Hundred Years' War** (England v. France; Joan of Arc) – 116 years |
| 1347–51 | **Black Death** (bubonic plague) in Europe |
| 14th c. | **Renaissance** begins in **Italy** (Florence) |
| c. 1440 | **Gutenberg** printing press |
| **1453** | **Fall of Constantinople** to the Ottomans |
| **1492** | **Columbus** reaches the Americas |
| **1498** | **Vasco da Gama** reaches **Calicut** |
| **1517** | **Martin Luther's 95 Theses** – Reformation |
| 1519–22 | **Magellan**–Elcano – first circumnavigation |
| 1618–48 | Thirty Years' War → Peace of Westphalia (1648) |

## 4. Age of revolutions
| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| **1688** | **Glorious Revolution** (England); Bill of Rights 1689 |
| 1760s → | **Industrial Revolution** begins in **Britain** (Watt's steam engine 1769) |
| **4 July 1776** | **American Declaration of Independence** (Jefferson); Treaty of Paris 1783 |
| **14 July 1789** | **French Revolution** – storming of the Bastille; 'Liberty, Equality, Fraternity' |
| 1804 / **1815** | Napoleon emperor / defeated at **Waterloo**; Congress of Vienna |
| 1848 | **Communist Manifesto** (Marx & Engels); revolutions across Europe |
| 1861 / 1870 | Kingdom of **Italy** (Mazzini, Garibaldi, Cavour) / Rome joined |
| 1861–65 | **American Civil War** (Lincoln); 13th Amendment ends slavery |
| 1868 | **Meiji Restoration**, Japan |
| 1869 | **Suez Canal** opened |
| **1871** | **Unification of Germany** (Bismarck) |
| 1911 | **Xinhai Revolution**, China (Sun Yat-sen) – end of the Qing |

## 5. World wars and the 20th century
| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| 28 June 1914 | Assassination of **Archduke Franz Ferdinand** at **Sarajevo** → **WW I** (1914–18) |
| 1917 | **Russian Revolution** – February; **October (Bolshevik, Lenin)** |
| **28 June 1919** | **Treaty of Versailles** (with Germany) |
| 1920 | **League of Nations** (Geneva) |
| 1922 | USSR formed; Mussolini in power in Italy |
| 1929 | **Great Depression** (Wall Street crash) |
| 1933 | Hitler becomes Chancellor of Germany |
| **1 Sept 1939** | Germany invades **Poland** → **WW II** |
| 7 Dec 1941 | **Pearl Harbor** – USA enters the war |
| 6 / 9 Aug 1945 | Atomic bombs on **Hiroshima / Nagasaki** |
| 24 Oct 1945 | **United Nations** founded |
| 1947 | India's independence; Marshall Plan; Cold War begins |
| 1949 | **NATO**; **People's Republic of China** (1 Oct, Mao) |
| 1950–53 | Korean War |
| 1955 | Warsaw Pact |
| 1957 | **Sputnik 1** (USSR) – space age |
| 1961 | **Gagarin** first in space; **Berlin Wall** built |
| 1962 | **Cuban Missile Crisis** |
| **20 July 1969** | **Moon landing** (Armstrong, Aldrin) |
| 1972 | **Stockholm Conference** on the Human Environment (UNEP) |
| 1987 | **Brundtland Report** 'Our Common Future' (sustainable development) |
| **9 Nov 1989** | **Fall of the Berlin Wall** |
| 3 Oct 1990 | German reunification; Aug 1990 Iraq invades Kuwait → Gulf War 1991 |
| **26 Dec 1991** | **Dissolution of the USSR** |
| 1992 | **Rio Earth Summit** – **Agenda 21** |
| 1993 / 1995 | **European Union** (Maastricht) / **WTO** |
| 1994 | End of apartheid – **Nelson Mandela** President |
| 1997 | Asian Financial Crisis; Kyoto Protocol |
| 11 Sept 2001 | 9/11 attacks in the USA |
| 2015 | **SDGs** (Agenda 2030) and **Paris Agreement** |

## 6. India-linked dates often mixed into world chronology
Bank nationalisation **1969** → LPG reforms **1991** → Asian Financial Crisis **1997**.

## 7. Traps
- Hundred Years' War lasted **116** years.
- Julius Caesar was **not** an emperor; **Augustus** was the first.
- Columbus (1492) came **before** Vasco da Gama (1498).
- Treaty of **Versailles** ended WW I (1919); Treaty of **Paris** (1783) ended the American war.
- Gagarin – first in space; Armstrong – first on the Moon.
